brief: How to write a brief somebody can act on

slots.eyebrow: On the page everything else depends on
slots.subtitle: Six things a brief has to contain before anybody can begin, and the one everybody leaves out.
slots.item1: Why a list of requirements is not a brief
slots.item2: The sentence that saves a month

slots.body: A brief that describes the solution has already made the expensive decision, usually by the person furthest from the work. Describing the change you want in the world leaves the method open to whoever knows it best.
slots.p1Body: What is different for somebody once this exists and works.
slots.p2Body: Every implementation detail in a brief is a constraint nobody argued for.

slots.body: Not a segment, not a persona — a person you could describe by their Tuesday. Broad audiences produce broad work, and broad work is the kind nobody remembers commissioning.
slots.p1Body: If two people want opposite things, you have two briefs.
slots.p2Body: What they are doing immediately before they encounter this.

slots.body: There is usually a launch, a board meeting or a season behind the date, and the date without its reason cannot be negotiated. A deadline you can explain is a deadline you can move.
slots.p1Body: The reason behind the date is what makes trade-offs possible.
slots.p2Body: Decided now, calmly, rather than in the last week under pressure.

slots.body: The exclusions do more work than the inclusions, because every unbilled hour and every late argument began as an assumption both sides held and neither wrote down.
slots.p1Body: What this deliberately does not cover, in plain words.
slots.p2Body: Agreeing a rate in advance turns an argument into an invoice.

slots.body: A brief with no named decision-maker produces work that is reviewed by everybody and approved by nobody, which is how a two-week project becomes a two-month one.
slots.p1Body: Committees do not decide, they schedule another conversation.
slots.p2Body: Booked before the work begins, not found afterwards.

slots.body: Without it, success is whatever the loudest person felt on the day of the review. With it, the argument happens now, in the calm, when changing your mind is still free.
slots.p1Body: Named in advance, even if it is rough and arguable.
slots.p2Body: A month after delivery, when the answer is actually available.

slots.body: What changes, who for, by when and why then, what is excluded, who decides, and how you will know. Anything longer is a document nobody finishes reading.
slots.signoff: The sixth sentence is the one that gets skipped
